issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: 'My body has been permanently damaged by what happened' implies an enduring physical injury theme, but the rest of the selected items do not support a bodily injury-focused combat presentation: memory items emphasize fragmentation/unreality, triggers emphasize intrusion/power imbalance, and strategies emphasize avoidance/hypervigilance rather than injury management. This appraisal is insufficiently anchored in the rest of the profile.

vignette: Emma, a 66-year-old divorced woman of Oceania descent, has been working as a Curriculum Designer for over four decades. Her life took an unexpected turn when she was deployed to a combat zone during her military service years ago. The trauma from that experience continues to shape her daily life and interactions. The traumatic event itself unfolded with shocking suddenness. Emma had been tasked with setting up a safe communication channel in a remote area when the base came under heavy fire. As chaos erupted, she watched helplessly as comrades were injured or killed around her. A helicopter made several low passes overhead, dropping supplies and medevac teams, but the noise of its rotors only added to the overwhelming cacophony of gunfire and explosions. Since then, Emma's world has been punctuated by sudden intrusions from that day. At home, in her quiet suburb, she would be out for a walk when a distant drone of an aircraft overhead would trigger a flood of memories. The sound of rotors spinning would plunge her back into the fear and helplessness she felt during those moments under fire. Emma had come to believe she was powerless in such situations, leading her to avoid places where she might encounter similar auditory triggers. She found herself increasingly isolated from others due to these avoidance behaviors; instead of attending social gatherings or going out for errands, she stayed home as much as possible. Even at work, Emma made a point to remain close to the exit during meetings, feeling a constant need to be ready to escape if something similar happened again. In her role as a Curriculum Designer, Emma's daily environment became another source of distress. She worked in an open office space, and the sounds of colleagues' conversations or the hum of machines often reminded her of the combat zone she had escaped. Her tendency to avoid feelings intensified at work; when faced with deadlines or challenging tasks that required emotional investment, she would retreat into a detached state, finding it difficult to fully engage with her job. Emma's memories of the event were fragmented and surreal. She knew what happened but found herself unable to articulate the sequence of events clearly. The memory was so extreme it felt almost unbelievable, as if it had been something that happened to someone else. This fragmentation made it even harder for her to process or integrate the experience into a coherent narrative. The weight of these experiences led Emma to develop strong negative appraisals about herself and her surroundings. She harbored deep self-doubt, questioning whether she could make the right decisions in critical situations. Her isolation only grew as she felt increasingly set apart from others who didn't understand or share her intense fears and memories. It was during a particularly overwhelming episode at work that Emma realized she needed help. A distant helicopter sound had triggered a panic attack while she was in a meeting, leading to a series of distressing flashbacks. She found herself unable to focus on anything else until she left the office abruptly. This incident, along with growing concerns about her declining performance and increasing isolation from colleagues, finally pushed Emma to seek professional assistance. What frightened her most was the prospect of never feeling safe again, always living in a state of hypervigilance where every sound or situation could trigger memories of that day. Yet, she was also hoping for a chance to reclaim her life, to find ways to manage and cope with these intrusive thoughts and feelings so that she could reconnect with others and regain control over her daily experiences. Emma's journey toward recovery is marked by the hope that through therapy, she can begin to rebuild her sense of self and trust in her ability to navigate the world without being consumed by the lingering echoes of her traumatic past.
